Legal Structure of PRIM", "node_id": "0001", "start_index": 5, "end_index": 7, "summary": "PRIM, established by Massachusetts in 1983, supervises the PRIT Fund, which invests assets of state and participating local retirement systems. Its nine-member board includes state officials, elected retirement-system representatives, and gubernatorial or treasurer appointees; appointed members serve four-year terms. PRIM’s mission is cost-effective funding of pension obligations while maximizing returns within acceptable risk. A legislated payment and investment-return schedule aims to fund Commonwealth obligations by 2040, assuming a 7% long-term actuarial return. The Board oversees policy, hires managers and advisors, and bears fiduciary responsibility; PRIT held about $96.6 billion at June 30, 2023. PRIM operates under MGL Chapter 32 and its Operating Trust, and is subject to conflict-of-interest and open-meeting laws. Advisory committees inform the Board; outside advisors support investment work, and BNY Mellon is custodian. The RFP seeks multi-asset credit managers for primarily non-investment-grade U.S. fixed income separate accounts.
